City Analysis

Six markets moving right now

Where the data points — and why it matters for your search.

Eagle Mountain

Median: $519,206 YoY: +4.3%

Eagle Mountain ranked as one of the fastest-growing cities in the entire United States for multiple years. The market has shifted: new-build oversupply means approximately 567 active listings and a more balanced environment. The draw remains: newer construction, lower entry price versus Lehi and Draper, and a young demographic profile bringing schools and retail. With supply up, buyers now have negotiating room — a sharp change from 2024–2025.

Saratoga Springs

Median: $527,450 Supply: ~6 months

At approximately six months of supply and 627 active listings, Saratoga Springs is the most buyer-friendly market on the northern Wasatch Front. Highridge subdivision listings are sitting at around 199 days on market. This is a genuine shift: sellers are negotiating, contingencies are back on the table, and inspection periods matter again. If you want time to think and room to negotiate, Saratoga Springs delivers that in August 2026.

Lehi

Median: $625,000 YoY: −0.4%

Lehi sits at the heart of Silicon Slopes. Adobe, Xactware, Qualtrics, and dozens of tech employers anchor the city. At $625K and $689K for single-family homes, it remains one of Utah's most expensive suburbs. The slight year-over-year decline reflects inventory normalization, not employer exodus. Approximately 444 active listings, around five months supply. Alpine District schools (8/10) keep families paying up.

St. George

Median: $517,500 Supply: ~5.2 months

St. George was the fastest-growing metro in the United States in 2021–2022, and remote-worker migration from California shows no sign of stopping. Washington County sits at approximately $545K median, 5.21 months supply. Inventory is looser than Salt Lake City but tighter than Denver. The trade: 300+ days of sunshine, red-rock desert scenery, and more negotiating room than the Wasatch Front.

South Jordan

SF Median: $925,000 Q2 2026

South Jordan sits at the convergence of two major employment corridors: the Bangerter Highway tech strip and the I-15 finance hub from Sandy to Draper. Employers like Goldman Sachs and eBay pull from South Jordan ZIP codes. Single-family in 84095 hit $925,000 in Q2, reflecting east-side Canyons District demand. The city has mature infrastructure: schools (Canyons 8/10, Corner Canyon HS 9/10), retail, parks. Stability over speculation.

Draper

SF Median: $925,000 Q2 2026

Draper anchors the I-15 tech and finance corridor. 1-800 Contacts, Fidelity, eBay, and dozens of mid-market software companies call it home. Single-family in 84020 reached $925,000 in Q2. The Point development (Phase 1 underway, for-sale vertical approximately 2028) will reshape the city's density and transit profile over the next decade. Canyons District schools (8/10), Corner Canyon outdoor access, and I-15 corridor employment make Draper one of Utah's most stable long-term markets.

Livability & Bikeability

How walkable is it, really?

Walk, bike, and transit scores out of 100, plus outdoor access. Editorial scores based on infrastructure, trail networks, and transit availability.

Utah is car-dependent outside Salt Lake City proper. Most suburbs score low on transit — factor in two-car household costs before you fall in love with a price. The bright spots: Daybreak remains Utah's most walkable master-planned community, Salt Lake City keeps adding protected bike lanes, and the 30-mile Provo River Parkway lifts Provo and Orem's bike score above their suburban peers.

Special Report · 2034 Winter Olympics

Salt Lake is hosting again

Salt Lake City is officially hosting the 2034 Winter Olympics — ceremonies at Rice-Eccles, events at the Delta Center, an athletes village downtown, and competition venues spread from Park City to Soldier Hollow. Estimates below are projections, not guarantees.

Direct Venue Host

Park City / Summit County

Utah Olympic Park, Deer Valley, Park City Mountain

Projected 15–22% appreciation by 2030

The primary venue host. Where the strongest, earliest price pressure lands.

Direct Venue Host

Salt Lake City

Rice-Eccles ceremonies, Delta Center events, downtown athletes village

Est. 10–16% uplift by 2030 based on 2002 precedent

Salt Lake City hosted in 2002; Wasatch Front values rose approximately 18% in the four years prior. The urban core captures strongest direct uplift.

Corridor Uplift

Draper / South Jordan

I-15 corridor — infrastructure spillover

Est. 6–10% uplift by 2030

Point-of-the-Mountain transit and road upgrades tied to the Games flow through these corridors.

Metro Overflow

Eagle Mountain / Saratoga Springs

50–55 min to venues

Est. 5–8% uplift by 2030 from metro overflow

Indirect but real: as venue-adjacent prices climb, priced-out buyers push demand to these markets.

The best window to buy near venues is now — before the 2028 construction phase triggers the next appreciation spike. All projections are estimates based on 2002 precedent and current market analysis.

Buyer's Guide

Utah first-time buyer programs

Money you may not know about — active programs as of August 2026

UHC FirstHome Loan

Up to 6%

Utah Housing Corporation's flagship loan pairs a competitive 30-year rate with down-payment and closing-cost assistance in one package. The most accessible entry point for most first-time buyers.

Min 620 FICO · Income limits apply by county

UHC Down Payment Assist

Up to $25,000

A second mortgage covering your down payment and closing costs. 30-year term at 1% above your first mortgage rate — no balloon payment, no large upfront obligation.

Min 620 FICO · Structured as second mortgage

Utah S.B. 240 New Construction

Up to $20,000

A legislature-funded grant for new builds — applicable to down payment, closing costs, or a permanent interest-rate buydown. Effective for buyers targeting Eagle Mountain or Saratoga Springs where new construction is abundant.

New construction only · First-time buyer required

Law Enforcement Grant

Up to $25,000

A grant — not a loan, no repayment — for active law-enforcement officers using a Utah Housing mortgage. Equals up to 3.5% of the purchase price. Quietly one of the most overlooked programs available.

Active law enforcement · UHC loan required

This Month

August 2026 market context

Mortgage Lock-In Effect

Gardner and Wood January 2026 forecast: Utah's housing market is "running in place." Approximately 61% of Utah mortgages are locked in under 4%, creating significant inventory constraints as homeowners resist trading up to 6.65% rates.

KUER, January 2026

Rental Market Shift

Utah County rents down approximately 5.6% year-over-year with 30% more rental listings. As for-sale inventory normalizes and rates stabilize, some would-be buyers are opting to rent and wait.

Realtor.com, 2026

The Point (Draper)

Phase 1 underway. For-sale vertical housing expected around 2028. Will reshape Draper's density and transit profile over the next decade as a major mixed-use development on former prison land.

Draper development updates, 2026

SB 284 ADU Law

Effective October 1, 2026: detached ADUs allowed on lots ≥11,000 sq ft. Cities may keep owner-occupancy requirements. Could gradually increase housing supply in established neighborhoods.

Utah Legislature, 2026
